newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin signs decree on Russian diamond exports.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin signs decree on Russian diamond exports.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree Monday giving Russia's dominant diamond producer, Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS), the right to sell rough diamonds to South Africa's De Beers which can then be exported.

The decree does not necessarily mean that a long-delayed gem deal between the two companies has been signed, but would appear to give the final go-ahead for the agreement. ARS and De Beers in Moscow were not immediately available for comment.

"The Russian government is to allow ... Almazy Rossii-Sakha, under conditions defined in accordance with the provisions of this decree, the right to sell to De Beers diamonds produced in Russia and meant for export," the decree said.
It also said Russia should adopt a proposal to work with the South African diamond cartel in the future on regulating volumes and prices of rough Russian diamonds sold on world markets.
An unnamed source at ARS was quoted by Prime Tass news agency as saying signing the trade deal between it and De Beers was now possible.

De Beers sharply curtailed the amount of diamonds it purchased from ARS at the end of 1996 after the Cabinet failed to approve a gem trade deal submitted in October 1996. Russia accounted for 26 percent of De Beers' total worldwide sales under the previous gem trade deal, which was worth around $1.2 billion a year to Russia.
